Validate gDR input data before import

Source: R/validate_input.R
validate_gdr_input.Rd

Checks a set of input files and reports every problem it finds, from unreadable files to plate-level anomalies in the readouts. Bench input (a manifest, treatment templates and raw plate-reader files) is loaded with load_data, so a failure reported for load_data is the error the import itself would raise. The checks also flag problems the loaders let through without an error: values in a Concentration sheet that are not numbers (those wells are dropped), raw plates without a barcode, duplicated wells, plates missing from the manifest or from the data, and Duration labels that do not fit the readouts of the control wells. PRISM input, processed MultiAssayExperiments and D300 files are recognised and checked too.

Usage

validate_gdr_input(
  paths,
  type = c("auto", "bench", "prism", "mae", "pre_d300"),
  instrument = NULL,
  id_patterns = list(drug = "^G[0-9]{8}", cellline = NULL),
  fix = FALSE,
  output_dir = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'gdr_validation'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

paths

character, paths to input files and/or directories. For a directory, the files directly inside it are used, not those in its subdirectories.

type

character, the kind of input: "auto" (detected from the files), "bench" (manifest, templates and raw plate-reader files), "prism", "mae" (a processed gDR MultiAssayExperiment saved as .qs2) or "pre_d300" (D300 .tdd files that still need import_D300).

instrument

character, the plate-reader format passed to load_data. When NULL, it is detected from the first raw file with detect_file_format.

id_patterns

list of regular expressions for identifier formats. drug is the format of a drug identifier once its batch suffix is removed (the default is the one gDRutils::remove_drug_batch uses), and cellline the format of a cell line identifier (no default). An element set to NULL switches its check off; elements left out keep their default.

fix

logical, whether to repair copies of the files in output_dir.

output_dir

character, a new or empty directory for the repaired copies; required with fix = TRUE.

x

a gdr_validation object.

...

not used.

Value

An object of class gdr_validation, a list with

verdict

"PASS", "WARN" or "FAIL", the most severe finding ("INFO" counts as "PASS").

data_type

the kind of input that was validated.

files

a data.table with one row per input file: file, path, role and format (the plate-reader format of raw files).

findings

a data.table with one row per finding: check, severity ("PASS", "INFO", "WARN" or "FAIL"), detail, fix_tier ("A" a mechanical fix, "B" a fix to confirm with whoever made the files, "C" a decision about the experiment, NA when there is nothing to fix) and status_code, the matching row of get_exception_data (NA when there is none).

fixes

character, one note per repair (empty without fix).

output_dir

the directory of the repaired copies, NA without fix. With fix = TRUE, files and findings describe the copies after the repairs.

Details

The input files are only read, never modified. With fix = TRUE they are copied to output_dir, the mechanical problems (fix tier "A") are repaired in the copies, and the copies are validated again: files re-encoded as UTF-8, spaces trimmed from file names, long tables saved as .tsv, Gnumber_1 and Concentration_1 sheets renamed, n/a and -99 cleared from templates, and manifest references that only differ from a template file by spaces or the extension rewritten. In xlsx files only the repaired cells change.

Examples

td <- get_test_data()
res <- validate_gdr_input(c(manifest_path(td), template_path(td), result_path(td)))
res$verdict
#> [1] "PASS"
res$findings
#>                 check severity
#>                <char>   <char>
#> 1:           manifest     PASS
#> 2:   combo_degenerate     INFO
#> 3:          load_data     PASS
#> 4: import_corrections     INFO
#> 5:    duplicate_wells     PASS
#> 6:   barcode_coverage     PASS
#> 7:     plate_outliers     INFO
#>                                                                                                                     detail
#>                                                                                                                     <char>
#> 1:                                                                                          Manifest loaded (12 plate(s)).
#> 2: Template(s) hold the second drug at a single dose, so the combination has no Drug 2 gradient: Template_7daytreated.xlsx
#> 3:                                                                           load_data() read 4608 readout(s) as EnVision.
#> 4:                                                                   load_data() changed the case of 320 untreated tag(s).
#> 5:                                                                                      No barcode and well is read twice.
#> 6:                                                          Every plate in the manifest has data, and the other way round.
#> 7:                                         Not checked: no group of 4 or more plates with the same Duration and cell line.
#>    fix_tier status_code
#>      <char>       <int>
#> 1:     <NA>          NA
#> 2:        C          NA
#> 3:     <NA>          NA
#> 4:     <NA>          NA
#> 5:     <NA>          NA
#> 6:     <NA>          NA
#> 7:     <NA>          NA

# repair copies of the files instead of only reporting
fixed <- validate_gdr_input(c(manifest_path(td), template_path(td), result_path(td)),
                            fix = TRUE, output_dir = tempfile())
fixed$fixes
#> character(0)
